mission: RUN WORKOUT STRUCTURE (Founder, 2026-11-13), request r3: make the Founder's binding product rule 'distance is the completion criterion of a native distance target; no automatic time ceiling; duration only an estimate; the athlete may always stop' sporting-safe (C1-C6). Branch claude/v1-run-workout-structure from c8104c1.

reviewer.role: Sports Science and Concurrent Training Reviewer (SSCTR), acting as decision author
reviewer.instance: A subagent instance dispatched by the Chief of this mission (model claude-opus-5-5, effort high). Whether it ran through the project native adapter cannot be verified from inside the run; no native dispatch is claimed. As far as it can tell this instance did not author SSCTR-RWS-R2-DECISION, SSCTR-RWS-DECISION-r1 or SSCTR-V1RC-DECISION-r1; it read them as standing records.
reviewer.nature: An AI software reviewer with no human credentials, licence, degree or registration and no clinical or legal equivalence. This record is an internal literature-based sporting decision, not human validation, empirical product validation or medical clearance.
reviewer.independence: Independent of the author of the request (the Chief). This instance authors the rulings and values below; it must not judge the implemented candidate or issue the V1X-RUN-NATIVE enabling record (SSCTR-08). No self-check is counted as independent approval.

authority: PROVISIONAL_INTERNAL_DOMAIN_AUTHORITY for bounded nonclinical sporting decisions only. Clinical judgment stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED. No runtime sovereignty, no Product Truth publication, no gate closure, no change to any frozen record, no boundary enabled. The Founder rule is a product decision recorded as given; this record does not reopen it.

fullTextReadThisRun: SRC-RWS3-01 Pobiruchin 2017 (PMC5350460): Methods (AIMS-certified half and full marathon courses), Analysis on recorded distance, Results on recorded distances by device category, Discussion and Limitations. Read in those passages.

SRC-RWS-07 Frandsen 2025 (PMC12421110): re-read this run in the abstract, the exposure definition (four states relative to the longest run of the previous 30 days), Table 1, and the sensitivity note that a 1% cut-off also associated increases of 1-10% with a higher injury rate.
SRC-RWS3-02 Bullock 2024 (PMC10797502): abstract, methods, Table 3 and the principal findings. Read in those passages; auxiliary only.

counterevidenceSearch: Attempted refutations: (1) 'Sizing at the band's slow edge is the conservative choice' - refuted for dose: the EASY and LONG bands are ceilings derived from fixed fractions (V1RC Q4) and are about 20-27% wide (r2 coverage sweep; r2 WE-10/WE-11 bands 325-410 and 380-460 s/km), so a distance sized at the slow edge plans only about 79-83% of the minutes for a runner at the ceiling and the 0.9 dose floor cannot hold; fixed fractions do not place individuals in one domain (V1RC:SRC08/SRC09), so an individual observed pace is the better sizing basis. (2) 'A 10% single-session distance increase is safe' - Frandsen 2025 used <=10% only as the reference category and reports that increases of 1-10% were also associated with a higher rate in a sensitivity analysis; 1.10 is therefore used only as an outer bound that the distance expression never exceeds, not as a safe threshold, and the engine's own minute ramp is not judged here. (3) 'GPS error is small on long runs' - on a certified half-marathon course watches had a mean absolute error of 0.6% but individual recordings ranged from 20.00 to 22.55 km (SRC-RWS3-01), and off-track wrist watches under-read by up to 9% (SRC-RWS-01): one automatic tolerance cannot cover both, hence two bounds and confirmation. (4) 'Self-report can replace measurement' - single-run self-reports have individual limits of agreement of -28% to +40% (SRC-RWS-08); weekly self-report agrees well with watches (ICC 0.88, SRC-RWS3-02), but those are weekly totals by watch wearers: confirmation is accepted only at the lowest evidence tier. (5) 'Running the same distance slower is riskier' - no study found either way (negative search); the residual is accepted with monitoring, not claimed safe.

sources.citation: Pobiruchin M, Suleder J, Zowalla R, Wiesner M. Accuracy and adoption of wearable technology used by active citizens: a marathon event field study. JMIR Mhealth Uhealth 2017;5(2):e24.
sources.findingsUsed: On AIMS-certified courses, recorded distances ranged from 20.00 to 22.55 km (half marathon) and 41.48 to 43.7 km (marathon); GPS sport watches had a mean absolute error of 0.12 km (0.6%) on the half marathon and phones 0.35 km (1.7%), overestimating; the authors note runners do not follow the ideal line, so part of the overestimation is real distance.
limitations: no per-device error on training routes
overestimation partly real path, not device error

sources.citation: Bullock G, Stocks J, Feakins B, Alizadeh Z, Arundale A, Kluzek S. Comparing self-reported running distance and pace with a commercial fitness watch data: reliability study. JMIR Form Res 2024;8:e39211.
sources.findingsUsed: 475 recreational runners, 3602 participant-weeks: weekly self-reported distance against Garmin data ICC 0.88 (good), pace ICC 0.72 (moderate), no discernible systematic bias.
limitations: participants wore the watch, so self-report may be informed by it

sources.citation: Frandsen JSB, Hulme A, Parner ET, et al. How much running is too much? Identifying high-risk running sessions in a 5200-person cohort study. Br J Sports Med 2025;59(17):1203-1210.
sources.findingsUsed: 5205 adult runners with GPS devices: relative to sessions up to 10% above the longest run of the previous 30 days (reference), single sessions >10-30% above it had a higher overuse-injury rate (adjusted HRR 1.64, 95% CI 1.31-2.05), >30-100% HRR 1.52 and >100% HRR 2.28; a sensitivity analysis with a 1% cut-off also associated 1-10% increases with a higher rate; acute:chronic and week-to-week ratios showed no or inverse associations.
limitations: distance may not be the optimal load measure (authors)

globalConditions.condition: Founder rule, recorded as given (product decision, not reopened): a native distance target is met by its distance; there is no automatic time ceiling as an alternative completion condition; duration is an estimate shown, never a completion criterion; the athlete may stop at any time; the real execution is recorded and a stop never counts as the target met; statuses DISTANCE, TIME, PARTIAL, STOPPED, UNKNOWN; absence of measurement is never success; absolute GPS precision is never demanded.

SSCTR-RWS-R2-DECISION global conditions RWS2-G.1 to RWS2-G.7 stand. In particular the planning dose (engine minutes) stays the only load the engine reads (G.1), and the TIME version stays available and is recommended in heat, hills, strong wind, on trail or on a treadmill (G.4).

Executed minutes, distance and status are recorded as real and read by the selector for the exposure rules of C1 and the format-fit rule X-2. They never enter an engine load sum, gate, ramp or taper (r2 G.1), and executed pace stays outside calibration except under the unchanged V1RC rules.

Effort governs. No text asks the athlete to speed up, to finish at any cost or to reach the distance by a time. Every distance session shows its estimated duration range as an estimate and says that stopping and walking are always allowed and are recorded as done.
Nothing here assesses eligibility in the clinical sense. Unknown eligibility stays ASK; symptoms use the existing warning-sign screen and clinical route; this record creates no clinical rule.

items.question: Exposure sizing of a distance target without a time ceiling: which pace sizes D for continuous runs and repetitions, and what excess over the planning minutes and over available time is acceptable.
items.ruling: APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS (continuous sizing CT-1 to CT-3) + KEEP (repetitions: r2 E1-E3, E5) + ABSTAIN (a numeric acceptable excess for execution slower than the sizing pace; replaced by the structural rules X-1 and X-2)
items.category: b on a (continuous: new rule over V1RC bands and P1, the R6 step and Frandsen); a (repetitions: r2 N2 unchanged); c (numeric excess: abstained)
items.summary: D is sized at the athlete's own slow pace, not at the ceiling and not at the band's slow edge. Sizing pace P_size = the slowest of: the P1 observed easy range's slow edge; the pace of the latest comparable run of the class (rounded up to 5 s); for a LONG run whose minutes equal the marathon cap (180, cap only), also the LONG band's slow edge; and never faster than P_typ. P_typ (the fastest compliant pace) = the slower of the class band's fast edge (ceiling) and the P1 observed median. D is the largest multiple of 1 km, else 0.5 km, with CT-1 D x P_size <= min(planning minutes, available minutes) (no planned excess), CT-2 D x P_typ >= 0.9 x planning minutes (dose floor, C6) and CT-3 D <= 1.10 x the longest run executed in the last 30 days. If none passes, the session is TIME. Repetitions keep r2: E1/E2 at the band edges, E3 budget, no time ceiling. Available time is covered by CT-1 for continuous runs and by E3 for repetitions. Execution slower than P_size can exceed the planning minutes; no number is supported for how much is acceptable, so the record abstains on a number and bounds it structurally: X-1 the latest run's pace enters the next sizing; X-2 two consecutive continuous sessions of a class with exposure above the estimate, a stop or a partial switch that class to TIME for 28 days.
changedFromProposal: The band's slow edge is not the default sizing pace: EASY and LONG bands are 20-27% wide ceilings, so sizing there plans about 79-83% of the minutes for a runner at the ceiling and cannot meet the 0.9 dose floor; it would send almost every session to TIME. It is used only for cap-bound marathon long runs.
The athlete's observed easy pace is required, not optional (see C2), and the latest comparable run of the class is added as a sizing source.
A distance bound tied to evidence is added (CT-3, Frandsen 2025).
The acceptable excess is abstained as a number and replaced by X-1/X-2.
RECOVERY_EASY and SHAKEOUT become time-only (see C2).
conditions: P1 is the V1RC P1 observed easy range of the session's week (3 to 5 qualifying easy runs in 28 days, at least 20 min, effort 4 or less, distance recorded, comparable conditions, no walk breaks), as V1RC computes it; never recomputed or widened.

Comparable run of the class (sizing source S3): the latest executed run of that class in the last 28 days with recorded minutes and distance, whatever its status, excluding TREADMILL, GPS flagged POOR, the V1RC notComparableConditions (HEAT, HILLY, TRAIL, WIND_STRONG) and stops for SYMPTOM. Its pace only ever slows P_size.

Longest run L30: the longest single executed run distance (any family, races included, any recorded source except none or GPS POOR) in the last 30 days; unknown L30 means TIME (DISTANCE_HISTORY_UNKNOWN).
EASY with strides: the run part is the planning minutes minus the strides block; CT-1 and CT-2 apply to the run part plus the block (as r2).
PROGRESSIVE_EASY (r2 N6) is sized exactly as CONTINUOUS_DISTANCE.
The estimate shown is [D x P_typ, D x P_size] minutes, labelled as an estimate.
Exposure above the estimate (record flag EXPOSURE_ABOVE_ESTIMATE): executed minutes > 1.015 x the high estimate. It is a record flag, not a status, not adverse and not a symptom.

X-2 counts only distance-expressed continuous sessions of one class (EASY or LONG) in sequence; a TIME session of that class executed without a stop resets the count; sessions flagged with a notComparable condition, treadmill sessions and UNKNOWN sessions neither count nor reset.
items.rationale: Without a ceiling the only exposure controls before the run are the size of D and who receives it. The band ceilings are deliberately loose (fixed fractions do not place individuals, V1RC:SRC08/SRC09), so a distance that is both dose-faithful and free of planned excess needs an individual pace range; P1 already gives one (median and slowest of the athlete's own easy runs) and the latest comparable run adds the class's own pace. CT-1 keeps the planned high estimate within the planning minutes and the athlete's available time; CT-2 keeps the dose floor; CT-3 keeps the distance expression inside the reference category of the largest prospective data on single-session distance increases (Frandsen 2025), without claiming that category is safe. What remains is execution slower than the athlete's own recent slow pace (walk breaks, fatigue, a hard day): no evidence quantifies an acceptable excess of duration at constant distance (negative search), so no number is set; X-1 makes the next sizing follow the slower execution and X-2 removes the distance expression when it repeatedly does not fit, both reversible.
items.evidenceStatusScope: SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS for individual-pace sizing (V1RC P1, V1RC:SRC08/SRC09) and for CT-3 as an outer bound (SRC-RWS-07); PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNCERTAIN for the acceptability of the residual slower-than-sizing excess, hence the abstention on a number.
items.confidenceReason: No study tests distance targets without a time limit in recreational runners; Frandsen is observational; the residual is bounded structurally, not quantified.
items.applicabilityLimits: Nonclinical recreational adults on roads or tracks (V1RC G.7), INTERMEDIATE or EXPERIENCED, EASY mode.

items.question: Eligibility for distance targets without a ceiling: who gets native distance continuous runs or repetitions and who gets time or mixed; does r2 N3 suffice without N4.
items.summary: r2 N3 suffices for repetitions and stays unchanged (NOVICE: even distance repeats with time recoveries only, the justified mixed form; INTERMEDIATE/EXPERIENCED: all patterns; phase lists; first exposure in TIME). It does not suffice for continuous runs once the ceiling is gone. A continuous distance target (EASY, LONG) also needs: INTERMEDIATE or EXPERIENCED; EASY mode; the P1 observed easy range AVAILABLE for the week; the class band AVAILABLE; L30 known; the class not paused by X-2. LONG also needs a comparable long run: an executed run in the last 28 days with actual minutes >= planning minutes - 5 (R6 longRunStepMinutes) and a recorded distance. RECOVERY_EASY and SHAKEOUT are time-only. NOVICE, unknown experience, WALK_JOG, RESTART, RETURN, ESTABLISHMENT, POST_EVENT and first exposure stay TIME for continuous runs; no new mixed continuous format is approved for NOVICE or RETURN.
changedFromProposal: The engine's longestContinuous is not used: it is the largest planned minutes of any run ever completed (r6-program.mjs 278-279), with no window and not executed; the requirement reads the executed run of the last 28 days (V1RC longestRunWithinDays 28) with its distance.
'With a band' is made concrete: the class band AVAILABLE and the P1 observed range AVAILABLE.

RECOVERY_EASY and SHAKEOUT leave the continuous-distance families: no individual recovery-pace observation exists, the RECOVERY ceiling is not the pace these runs are run at, and their purpose is low exposure, so a distance adds excess risk with no dose benefit.
conditions: Experience as the engine stores it; unknown is NOVICE (r2).

After a RETURN or RESTART ends, continuous runs stay TIME until V1RC again reports a P1 observed range and the class band is AVAILABLE; repetitions return to native only when their band is AVAILABLE (V1RC withdrawal rules unchanged).
First LONG of a plan, or a LONG step more than one engine step above the latest executed run: TIME (LONG_HISTORY_NOT_COMPARABLE).
Eligibility here is sporting eligibility for an expression only; it never changes the dose, the engine's family choice or any clinical route.
items.rationale: The Founder rule itself allows time or justified mixed sessions for novices and returning athletes. The remaining question is who can carry a distance with no ceiling: the athlete whose own recent continuous pace is known (P1) and, for long runs, who has run nearly this long within the last four weeks, so that both the sizing pace and the distance reference are individual and current. Frandsen's 30-day longest-run reference supports reading recent executed history rather than lifetime planned minutes.

items.question: What target met is, by measurement source; tolerances; role of athlete or device-lap confirmation; the 15.6 km versus confirmed 16 km conflict; which steps count.
items.ruling: APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS + ABSTAIN (a GPS tolerance for single repetitions)
items.category: b (continuous tolerances tied to evidence) + a (r2 N7 lap rule for repetitions) + c (per-repetition GPS tolerance: abstained)
items.summary: Counted steps: WORK steps for repetition sessions; the main run for continuous sessions; warm-up, cool-down, recoveries and strides are never required. Continuous runs by source: TRACK or measured course - counted distance >= target, no tolerance. GPS (quality not POOR) - measured >= 0.97 x target is met (tier GPS) with or without confirmation; from 0.91 to below 0.97 it is met only with the athlete's confirmation (tier CONFIRMED), otherwise PARTIAL and one ASK; below 0.91 with confirmation it is UNKNOWN (MEASUREMENT_CONFLICT) with an ASK through the record's correction path, without confirmation PARTIAL. GPS POOR - the measurement is kept but not used: confirmation is met (tier MANUAL), otherwise UNKNOWN. TREADMILL - display >= target is met (tier TREADMILL), otherwise PARTIAL. MANUAL - an entered distance >= target or an explicit confirmation is met (tier MANUAL); an entered distance below 0.97 x target without confirmation is PARTIAL. No measurement and no confirmation - UNKNOWN. Repetitions: r2 N7 stands - a WORK step is met by an athlete lap or a device lap (an auto-lap at the target distance is a device lap); GPS distance never decides a repetition and no GPS tolerance is set for it; no lap and no confirmation makes that step UNKNOWN. The tier never changes progression credit; it only feeds V1RC pace evidence (unchanged) and Data/G03 reporting.
conditions: The 15.6 km of 16 km case is 0.975 x target: met by measurement (tier GPS); the confirmation is recorded but not needed.
The classification is applied after the run; it never shortens the live target. The athlete is never asked to run extra to make a watch match, and never told a run is met early.

A MEASUREMENT_CONFLICT is not adverse and not a refusal of the athlete's word: the athlete may correct the source (for example a measured course or poor GPS) through the existing correction path; the correction then classifies under its source.
Over-distance is recorded as executed and is DISTANCE; it enters L30 and the exposure flags like any execution.
Treadmill completion counts for the session but never for pace evidence (V1RC); the TIME version stays the recommended choice on a treadmill (r2 G.4).
TIME-expressed sessions keep the engine's existing completion read unchanged (status TIME).
items.rationale: 0.97 lies below the smallest per-area mean absolute percentage error of eight wrist watches (3.2%, SRC-RWS-01) and above the mean absolute error of watches (0.6%) and phones (1.7%) on a certified half-marathon course (SRC-RWS3-01), so most faithful executions read met without asking. 0.91 is the largest documented under-reading (up to 9% off-track, SRC-RWS-01); between the two bounds device error alone can explain the shortfall, so the athlete's confirmation decides; below 0.91 a good-quality measurement contradicts the confirmation beyond documented device error, so the honest status is UNKNOWN until the athlete corrects the source. Confirmation without any measurement is accepted only at the lowest tier because single-run self-reports have wide individual limits of agreement (SRC-RWS-08). Repetitions are too short for the validated range (SRC-RWS-03; no repetition-scale validation found), so the lap remains the completion test as in r2.
items.confidenceReason: Device validation is single-participant (SRC-RWS-01), an older device generation (SRC-RWS3-01) or continuous track runs (SRC-RWS-02); no study validates confirmation behaviour.
items.applicabilityLimits: Road or track running; trail and treadmill per conditions; continuous-run tolerances only for continuous runs.

items.question: STOPPED: reasons, missing reason, SYMPTOM routing, effect on progression, repeated stops.
items.category: a (V1RC P3 stop reasons and R-01, existing warning-sign screen and review kinds) + b (FATIGUE, CHOICE, format-fit counter)
items.summary: Reasons: SYMPTOM, FATIGUE, PACING, CONDITIONS, TIME, CHOICE, OTHER. A stop with no reason is read as SYMPTOM (V1RC R-01). SYMPTOM opens the existing warning-sign screen (WARNING_SIGN_SCREEN_REQUIRED keeps run sessions in TIME until it is answered; any yes takes the existing clinical route). FATIGUE is offered as the existing SYSTEMIC_FATIGUE review, which stays behind the existing screen under the V1RC q11 conditions. PACING, CONDITIONS, TIME, CHOICE and OTHER are recorded only. Every STOPPED session is not complete: the engine's partial semantics apply (no ADVANCE, no EARNED; the step holds). Executed distance and time are recorded as real. Repeated stops: repetitions keep r2 N10 (the next session at that step uses even repeats); continuous classes use X-2; repeated SYMPTOM stops follow the existing screen's persistence routes. No new clinical rule.
conditions: The stop can be declared during the run or afterwards; the athlete picks one reason; no justification is asked beyond it.
No wording treats a stop as failure; the plan text says stopping is always allowed.
A SYMPTOM stop never feeds sizing (C1 S3) and never counts as a compatible response.
FATIGUE is never itself read as illness or as clearance; it never enters ADVANCE, EARNED or calibration (V1RC q11).
items.rationale: The reasons and the missing-reason reading reuse the approved V1RC test rules; FATIGUE and CHOICE are additions that only record and route to existing paths. Holding progression after an unmet target keeps the engine's existing meaning of a partial session and never turns a stop into an earned step.
items.confidenceReason: Reuses approved rules and existing routes; the only added number is the two-session counter tied to V1RC consecutiveSessionsRequired.

items.question: PARTIAL and UNKNOWN semantics.
items.summary: PARTIAL: a known execution below the target with no stop declared (14 of 16 km; 5 of 6 repetitions): not complete, the step holds, the existing PARTIAL_SESSION review applies, and one non-blocking ASK offers the stop reasons; an answer turns it into STOPPED with that reason and its routes; no answer keeps PARTIAL and is not read as SYMPTOM, because no stop was declared. UNKNOWN: completion cannot be established (no measurement and no confirmation, or a measurement conflict): not complete, not adverse, no symptom read, the step holds, not counted by X-2; the athlete can confirm later through the record's correction path, which reclassifies under the existing provenance rules. Session status precedence: STOPPED, then PARTIAL, then UNKNOWN, then met (DISTANCE when any WORK target is a distance, TIME when all are time).
conditions: UNKNOWN is never success (Founder rule) and never failure.
A later correction does not silently rewrite a decision already taken from the earlier read; the existing correction path and its provenance rule decide what a later review reads.
items.rationale: Separating a declared stop (R-01 applies) from a known shortfall without a declaration avoids reading every imported short run as a symptom while still offering the symptom route at the one ASK. UNKNOWN keeps absent evidence from being counted either way.

items.question: Envelope re-tie: keep [0.9, 1.015] as a dose tolerance; remove E4 for distance sessions.
items.summary: E1 and E2 keep [0.9, 1.015] at the band edges as a planning dose tolerance. 1.015 stays tied to the V1RC on-band fraction. 0.9 is re-tied from the engine's completion read to dose parity with the TIME expression: the engine credits a TIME session delivered at 0.9 of its minutes, so a native format never plans less work, at the fastest allowed pace, than a TIME session the engine would credit. E3 and E5 unchanged. E4 is removed as a sporting requirement for every session completed by distance (native repetition formats and continuous distance); for continuous runs CT-2 is the dose floor. r2's 'a continuous run ended at the time ceiling counts as met' and 'a runner far faster than the band may be read partial' are superseded.
conditions: Engineering/QRE: a DISTANCE-met session must not be read partial by the engine's minutes read (r6-adaptation.mjs:195). If the integration cannot achieve that without a frozen edit, E4 may stay as an engineering compatibility check (it only removes formats; sporting-neutral). The selector never fabricates minutes.
items.rationale: The values keep their meaning for the planned dose; only their justification changes, because completion no longer uses minutes for distance sessions.
items.applicabilityLimits: Native formats only; EQUIVALENT keeps r1.

continuous.definition: one easy-domain run of D km; completion by distance (values.completion); no time ceiling; the estimated duration range is shown as an estimate
continuous.planningMinutes: canonical durationMinutes M (EASY with strides: run part = M - strides block minutes)
continuous.availableMinutes: the athlete's declared minutes for the session as the engine stores them: schedule.longRunMinutes for LONG, schedule.runMinutes for EASY
continuous.paceTypical: P_typ = max(class band fastSecondsPerKm, P1 observed range fastSecondsPerKm (median))

paceSizingSources.S2: LONG only: pace of the comparable long run (values.eligibility.continuous.LONG), rounded up to 5 s, unless TREADMILL or condition-flagged
paceSizingSources.S3: pace of the latest executed run of the same class in the last 28 days with recorded minutes and distance, any status, rounded up to 5 s; excluded: TREADMILL, GPS POOR, HEAT, HILLY, TRAIL, WIND_STRONG, STOPPED for SYMPTOM
paceSizingSources.S4: LONG only, when M equals the marathon cap (180, cap only): the LONG band slowSecondsPerKm

continuous.paceSizing: P_size = max(P_typ, S1, S2, S3, S4) over the sources present (seconds per km; max = slowest)
continuous.distanceKm: the largest multiple of 1 km, else of 0.5 km, that passes CT-1, CT-2 and CT-3

checks.CT-1: D x P_size / 60 (+ strides block) <= min(M, availableMinutes)
checks.CT-2: D x P_typ / 60 (+ strides block) >= 0.9 x M
checks.CT-3: D <= 1.10 x L30, L30 = longest single executed run distance in the last 30 days (any family, races included; sources TRACK, OFFICIAL, GPS not POOR, TREADMILL, MANUAL)

continuous.estimate: [D x P_typ / 60, D x P_size / 60] minutes (+ strides block), labelled estimate

exposure.flag: EXPOSURE_ABOVE_ESTIMATE when executed actual.minutes > 1.015 x estimate high
exposure.X-1: the latest executed run of the class enters the next sizing as S3 (only ever slower)
exposure.X-2: two consecutive distance-expressed continuous sessions of the same class, each with EXPOSURE_ABOVE_ESTIMATE, STOPPED (any reason) or PARTIAL: that class is TIME for 28 days from the second (reason CONTINUOUS_FORMAT_PAUSED)
exposure.X-2.counting: a TIME session of the class executed without a stop resets the count; sessions flagged HEAT, HILLY, TRAIL or WIND_STRONG, TREADMILL sessions and UNKNOWN sessions neither count nor reset
exposure.engineLoad: executed minutes never enter an engine load sum, gate, ramp or taper (r2 G.1)

aeReview.1_adequate: The planning dose and the engine's choices stay as they are (r2 G.1); only the expression and its completion change.
aeReview.2_materialFact: The Founder's product rule removes the ceiling; the material sporting fact is that execution can now exceed the planning minutes.
aeReview.3_keepDefensible: Keeping r2 N4 is not available (Founder). Keeping r2's ceiling-sized D without the ceiling is not defensible: sized at the ceiling, every slower runner exceeds M.
aeReview.4_changeNecessary: Yes, relative to r2 N4 without its ceiling.
aeReview.5_smallest: Individual sizing pace, one distance bound, one exposure flag and a two-session pause; no new number beyond tied values.
aeReview.6_smallerInsufficient: Sizing at the band slow edge fails the dose floor for nearly all athletes; sizing at the ceiling leaves unbounded excess; eligibility alone leaves slow days unaddressed.
aeReview.7_priority: Progression is credited by distance as the Founder rule says; stops and partials hold; nothing is earned from a stop.
aeReview.8_evidence: Supported with limits for individual sizing and measurement tolerances; the residual is plausible but uncertain, so no number is set.
aeReview.9_uncertainty: Acceptability of a slower-than-sizing execution; coverage; confirmation behaviour.
aeReview.10_askHoldClinical: ASK for PARTIAL and for measurement conflicts; existing screen for SYMPTOM; no CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED item arises.

changedFromProposal: C1: individual sizing pace instead of the band slow edge; CT-3 added; numeric excess abstained, X-1/X-2 added.
C2: executed 28-day comparable long run instead of engine longestContinuous; P1 required; RECOVERY_EASY and SHAKEOUT time-only.
C3: two GPS bounds (0.97 automatic, 0.91 with confirmation) with MEASUREMENT_CONFLICT below; repetitions keep the lap rule with no GPS tolerance.
C4: FATIGUE routed to the existing SYSTEMIC_FATIGUE review; X-2 for repeated continuous stops.
C5: PARTIAL gets one ASK and is not read as SYMPTOM without a declared stop.
C6: as proposed, with 0.9 re-tied to dose parity and an engineering compatibility condition on E4.

supersedesInR2.RWS-N4: history only (rejected by the Founder); its continuous values are replaced by values.continuous here
supersedesInR2.RWS-N7: the continuous parts (ceiling counts as met; faster runner read partial) are superseded; the repetition lap rule stands
supersedesInR2.RWS-N1: RECOVERY_EASY and SHAKEOUT leave the native catalog

abstentions: A numeric acceptable excess of executed minutes over the planning minutes for execution slower than the sizing pace (C1): no evidence; structural rules X-1/X-2 instead.
A GPS distance tolerance for single repetitions (C3): no repetition-scale validation; the lap decides as in r2.
New mixed continuous formats for NOVICE or RETURN athletes (C2).
Whether running a given distance slower than planned changes injury or overreaching risk (negative search).

escalations.text: No part of the rule was judged unsafe for an eligible population, and no clinical item arises. Making it safe has product consequences: continuous distance targets reach only INTERMEDIATE/EXPERIENCED athletes with recent qualifying easy runs (V1RC P1); long runs also need a run of nearly that length in the last 4 weeks; recovery runs and shakeouts stay in time; marathon long runs at the 180-min cap will mostly be time; a long run run much slower than usual makes the next long run a time session, and two in a row pause distance for that run type for 28 days. The accepted residual is that a run executed slower than the athlete's own recent slow pace lasts longer than planned; it is bounded by these rules, not by a number. A numeric bound would need a time ceiling (rejected by the Founder), evidence that does not exist, or funded human review.

Update handoff sections 3-5: no ceiling on continuous distance steps; completion by status with sources and tiers (values.completion, values.statuses); stop reasons and routes; the new suppression reasons and order; RECOVERY_EASY and SHAKEOUT time-only; E4 scope; the estimate range from P_typ/P_size.

Wording of the estimate and the stop-any-time line; neutral status wording; a stop control with the seven reasons; the one ASK for PARTIAL and for MEASUREMENT_CONFLICT; the TIME-version recommendation.
Statuses, evidence tiers, MEASUREMENT_CONFLICT, correction path and EXPOSURE_ABOVE_ESTIMATE; planned versus executed distance or minutes is not an adherence measure.

(1) The engine's minutes read must not mark a DISTANCE-met session partial, or E4 stays as a compatibility check (C6). (2) T3: steps, formatHash, status, stop reason, measurement source, GPS quality, confirmation and executed minutes and distance must survive in actualLedger. (3) P1, S2/S3, L30 and X-2 read recorded rows under the existing provenance rules, deterministically. (4) Coverage sweep on the candidate. (5) The 0.97/0.91 classification applies to continuous runs only.

In the TIME expression the engine's 5-min long-run step is an increase above 10% for long runs under 50 min; SRC-RWS-07 associates single-session distance increases above 10% (and, in sensitivity, 1-10%) with a higher overuse-injury rate. Not a ruling and not reopened here; listed as a re-review trigger.
No new clinical rule; SYMPTOM and FATIGUE use existing routes.
